---
title: "Desktop Beta Distribution"
description: "Build, verify, and publish Windows, macOS, and Linux beta packages without exposing signing credentials."
---

`tuturuuu.com/download` lists iOS/TestFlight and Android/Google Play early access,
plus verified desktop packages from GitHub Releases. Every distribution is beta
and may not be production-ready. Mobile users may need an invitation using their
Apple or Google account; installing TestFlight alone does not grant access.

## Release workflow

`.github/workflows/desktop-beta.yaml` runs on relevant production pushes or an
explicit dispatch from `production`. Desktop publication is opt-in: keep the
repository variable `DESKTOP_BETA_ENABLED` unset until signing and platform
verification are ready. While disabled, the workflow reports **coming soon** and
does not publish; this is a deferred release, not a successful desktop rollout.
Set it to `true` only after completing the prerequisites below.
Set repository variable `DESKTOP_BETA_PLATFORMS` to a comma-separated subset of
`windows,macos,linux` (default: all three). Selected platforms build concurrently.
Linux can ship while another platform completes signing setup.
The `desktop-beta` GitHub environment owns the release configuration. Publication
can publish the successfully verified selected-platform subset; failed platforms
remain unavailable. Present invalid assets block publication rather than being
dropped. Missing certificates never permit unsigned Windows or macOS packages.

Build inputs contain only allowlisted public URLs, publishable Supabase keys,
OAuth client IDs, and feature flags. `DESKTOP_PUBLIC_CONFIG` is a JSON environment
variable, validated by `scripts/desktop-deployment/public-config.mjs`. Never use a
general `.env` file or a Supabase service-role key as a Dart define. The validator
rejects unknown fields and elevated JWTs without logging their values.

Signing credentials are available only to their OS-specific packaging step,
after Flutter compilation. They are never passed into Turbo, Flutter, a source
archive, or an artifact path.

| Platform | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PFX_B64`, `WINDOWS_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` secrets: trusted Authenticode code-signing certificate with private key. |
| macOS | `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_B64`, `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` secrets: **Developer ID Application** certificate, not the App Store distribution certificate. |
| macOS identity | `MACOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` environment variables identifying the intended Developer ID signer. |
| Notarization | `APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_ID`, `APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID`, `APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY_P8_B64` secrets. |

Keep source signing material in the dedicated encrypted Infrastructure desktop
vault. Desktop jobs use protected environment secrets by default; the explicit
vault opt-in obtains only the matching platform's approved material through its
separate desktop OIDC contract. Never use the mobile bundle endpoint or token for
desktop jobs. Certificate issuance, rotation, and identity verification remain
prerequisites for a real release.

## Packages and trust

- Windows: per-user Inno Setup installer with timestamped Authenticode signatures.
  The installer registers and removes the browser-login callback protocol.
- macOS: universal Apple silicon/Intel DMG. The app and image are Developer ID
  signed, notarized, stapled, and assessed. Temporary keychain/P12/API-key files
  are removed in `finally` cleanup.
- Linux: Ubuntu 24.04+ amd64 `.deb`, containing the Flutter runtime dependencies
  and desktop protocol registration. Install through a package manager so system
  dependencies are resolved. GitHub provenance and checksums cover the package.

`audit-bundle.mjs` scans the built app before packaging for credential files,
private-key/token markers, service-role JWTs, and links escaping the bundle.
This is an additional check, not a substitute for keeping secrets out of builds.
Signing receipts bind the Windows and macOS verification to the package hash,
source SHA, and workflow run. Publication rejects extra files, missing selected platforms,
or mismatched receipts.

Actions artifacts expire after seven days and are intended for CI inspection.
Public downloads use persistent GitHub Release assets, which do not require a
repository token in the browser. The workflow attests the packages and verifies
each signed attestation against the exact source SHA, protected `production` ref,
desktop workflow identity, and GitHub-hosted runner policy before it uploads a
draft `desktop-v<version>-<run-id>` prerelease, then makes the complete selected-platform prerelease
visible. It never marks the desktop beta as the repository's latest stable
release or overwrites an existing release tag. A failed draft needs inspection
before rerunning; do not replace assets of a published tag.

Draft publication resolves the authenticated `gh release view` database ID and
reads the release by REST ID; the release-by-tag endpoint can return 404 for an
existing draft. Before making the prerelease visible, the publisher checks the
resolved ID, exact expected tag and source SHA, draft/prerelease flags, and the
complete owned asset names, upload states, and SHA-256 digests. A lookup or
identity mismatch leaves publication blocked. The actual publisher's mocked-CLI
404 and mismatch regressions run with
`node --test scripts/desktop-deployment/publish.test.mjs`; no release is written
by those tests.

The download page caches public release metadata for five minutes and sends
package downloads directly to GitHub's CDN. It validates the exact repository,
tag format, filenames, uploaded state, positive sizes, and GitHub SHA-256 digests.
Each platform uses its latest verified release independently. Unavailable platforms show an honest unavailable state with a web-app
alternative; they never produce guessed download URLs.

## Verification

Local validation stays limited to non-build checks and is admitted through the
resource queue:

```sh
ttr resources status --json
ttr resources run -- node --test scripts/desktop-deployment/*.test.mjs
ttr resources run -- bun check:mobile
```

Run focused Infrastructure route, operator UI and source TypeScript checks when
those surfaces change. Do not run `bun check`, `bun setup`, app/package builds, or
native release builds locally. Require the applicable app and desktop release
builds in CI for the exact source commit. `prepare-macos.mjs` is runner preparation
that rewrites Firebase metadata and copies the selected flavor plist; it is not a
read-only verification command.

Before publishing, verify installation, browser sign-in callbacks, workspace
isolation, resizing, and core app flows on each supported OS. A passing macOS build
does not prove Windows/Linux runtime compatibility. Linux CI installs the generated package,
waits for a visible first-frame window under Xvfb, and checks that a harmless
browser callback activation leaves the app running. This smoke check does not
prove authenticated sign-in or interactive Polkit updates. Never label missing platform
runtime or signing verification as complete.

The separate `mobile-build-windows.yaml` development check runs Flutter setup
without an Actions cache. If its Windows job remains in `Post Setup Flutter`
after the artifact upload, inspect the exact job and rerun that workflow on the
same commit. The post-job cache upload is not evidence that the build failed.

## Automatic desktop updates

Published desktop builds include `DESKTOP_RELEASE_RUN_ID`, supplied directly by
`desktop-beta.yaml`. Development builds and mobile store builds do not run the
desktop updater. The version and run ID together distinguish successive beta
builds without manually changing Release Please versions.

On startup and every six hours, the app checks the public GitHub release list and
automatically downloads a newer desktop beta for its platform. Downloads use no account
session or repository token. Exact repository URLs, prerelease tags, every present
platform asset, byte counts, and GitHub SHA-256 digests are required. Redirects
are limited to GitHub's HTTPS asset hosts. Incomplete downloads never become
installable, and cached packages are rehashed before use. After verification, older
updater-owned release cache directories are pruned; unrelated files are preserved.

When ready, a compact banner offers **Install and restart** or **Install on next
launch**. Next-launch consent applies only to that exact release and can be
cancelled. A failed installation clears the saved choice so startup cannot get
stuck retrying it. Offline checks and download failures leave the current app
usable and retry on the next check.

- Windows verifies Authenticode on both the running executable and installer,
  requires matching certificate subjects, waits for the old process to exit,
  and runs the per-user Inno installer. A successful installation relaunches the
  app. The helper rechecks the digest and signatures immediately before running.
- macOS verifies the signed/notarized disk image, validates the replacement app's
  signature and matching Apple team, and stages it on the destination volume
  before exiting. The helper swaps bundles after exit and keeps the previous
  app in one updater-owned recovery directory. An unwritable installation
  directory or running directly from a mounted disk image blocks installation
  while keeping the app open.
- Linux asks the operating system's Polkit agent to authorize a packaged,
  root-owned helper. It stages and verifies the archive in a root-owned directory,
  then uses `apt-get install` to resolve dependencies. An unprivileged detached
  helper waits for the previous process to exit before relaunching
  `/opt/tuturuuu/tuturuuu`. The Flutter process never runs as root. A cancelled
  elevation prompt leaves the current app open. Linux beta installations require
  Ubuntu 24.04+ amd64, `pkexec`, and a desktop Polkit agent.

Before enabling publication, exercise installation and at least one subsequent
update on each actual supported OS, including cancelled elevation, damaged
packages, next-launch consent, and relaunch. Unit tests for the metadata and
transport boundary do not establish native installer success.

### Current provisioning prerequisites

The existing Infrastructure mobile vault supports Android/iOS bundles and binds
its OIDC audience to the mobile store workflow. Its App Store distribution P12
is **not** a macOS Developer ID certificate, and the desktop workflow cannot use
that bundle endpoint under the mobile workflow's identity. Provision the desktop
credentials listed above through the separate desktop vault and protected
environment-secret or explicit vault workflow path; do not copy a mobile CI
token into desktop jobs or weaken that OIDC policy. A Microsoft Store developer
account alone does not supply the Authenticode certificate used by this workflow.

## Windows Store draft channel

`desktop-store-draft.yaml` is a manual build. Its default production-only mode produces an
unsigned MSIX artifact for the reserved **Tuturuuu** product (`9N7B6VC7RR7W`),
using the exact Partner Center package name and publisher from
`windows-store-manifest.xml`. Microsoft signs packages distributed through the
Store. This job does not upload or submit an app for certification. It signs a separate
temporary copy with a runner-local certificate, installs it, verifies the package
identity and visible first frame, and exercises a harmless browser callback. The
unsigned submission artifact is unchanged; the test package and certificate are
removed afterward. WACK runs when the kit and an interactive session are present.
A missing kit/session writes an explicit submission-blocked report and fails the
submission job, preventing MSIX upload. Only an explicit diagnostic-only run may
finish with blocked evidence; it never uploads a submission MSIX. When WACK runs,
a failed, missing, or non-passing report fails either mode. Inspect the attached
validation reports before submission. The prerequisite policy is covered by
`store-certification-gate.test.mjs`; actual PowerShell execution and WACK remain
Windows CI gates, not evidence established by source-policy tests on another OS.

For pre-promotion diagnostics, dispatch this workflow on `main` with
`diagnostics_only=true`. The job uses the separate `desktop-diagnostics` environment,
restricted to the `main` branch and containing only `DESKTOP_PUBLIC_CONFIG`. Keep
`desktop-beta` restricted to `production`; do not copy signing secrets into the
diagnostics environment. A branch-policy rejection happens before runner allocation
and produces no build or certification logs. It runs the same production-channel build, installed-app
smoke, and strict certification checks, but uploads only validation evidence.
It never uploads the submission MSIX, submits to Partner Center, or publishes a
beta. Main without this explicit input and all other branches are skipped.
This permits investigation of certification blockers before production sync;
a diagnostics run is not evidence that production or Store distribution changed.

Store builds omit `DESKTOP_RELEASE_RUN_ID`: the Store manages their updates,
while the direct EXE installer remains a separate certificate-backed channel.
The MSIX package version uses major/minor plus the dedicated workflow run number,
with a zero revision required by Store submissions; app display versions remain
managed by Release Please. The run number must fit the MSIX 16-bit component.

Before submission, validate on Windows with Windows App Certification Kit and
verify packaged browser sign-in callbacks, media permissions, file selection,
installation, and Store upgrades. Complete truthful listing screenshots, privacy
and data declarations, age rating, restricted `runFullTrust` justification, and
reviewer access instructions. The current product is a draft and its Store link
must not be advertised as an available download until Microsoft approves it.

### Linux update trust

Linux beta packages trust the protected GitHub release and its asset digest; they
do not carry a separate publisher signature. Compromise of that release authority
can compromise an accepted Linux update. Polkit asks for installation consent. The
root-owned packaged helper copies the selected archive into a private root-owned
staging directory, rechecks its digest and package identity there, and installs it
with apt so dependencies are resolved. It never installs the user-writable cache
path directly. macOS and Windows additionally require OS publisher signatures.

### Verify downloaded desktop packages

Every platform package has cryptographically signed GitHub provenance. Verify a
package before installing it using GitHub CLI and the exact source SHA recorded
in that release's notes:

```sh
gh attestation verify ./Tuturuuu-linux-x64.deb \
  --repo tutur3u/platform \
  --signer-workflow tutur3u/platform/.github/workflows/desktop-beta.yaml \
  --source-ref refs/heads/production \
  --source-digest <release-source-sha> \
  --deny-self-hosted-runners
```

Use the downloaded `.dmg` or `.exe` path to verify those platforms. The workflow
runs the same verification before publication and blocks the whole selected
release if any signature, artifact digest, or workflow identity fails.
Linux's signed provenance covers the exact Debian archive; it is not an embedded
Debian publisher signature and the current Linux updater does not independently
verify provenance. Windows and macOS additionally enforce native publisher trust.
Do not describe receipt hashes alone as cryptographic signature verification.

Windows direct distribution requires a trusted Authenticode certificate. A
Microsoft account or Store registration alone is insufficient. Microsoft Artifact
Signing is an alternative managed signing provider: it requires an accessible
Azure subscription, completed identity validation, and a certificate profile,
plus a narrowly scoped CI workload identity. Its non-exportable signing key is
not a PFX to retrieve from an account. Keep Windows unavailable until a supported
signing provider is configured and CI verifies the actual installer signature.

## Failed platform builds

Platform builds run independently. If one fails, the publication job may still
publish the successful platforms after exact run/source/hash receipts and signed
provenance verification. A present but incomplete or invalid package blocks
publication; missing failed platforms remain unavailable. Cancelled workflows do
not publish. The workflow itself remains failed so the platform problem stays
visible.

macOS signing failures report only a fixed stage name, such as certificate import,
artifact signing, notarization, or Gatekeeper assessment. Private command arguments,
stdout and stderr remain suppressed. Check the named provider stage without
posting credentials or weakening the signing gates.

## Infrastructure desktop status

The root workspace's Infrastructure **Desktop deployment** page shows public
production beta workflow jobs and the latest published artifact for each platform.
A checksum or release entry is metadata, not independent signature verification.
The explicit provenance step is reported only when that step passed in the shown
run; artifacts from earlier runs remain separate. Provider configuration stays
unknown because private signing credentials are never queried or exposed.

Secure management links open the protected GitHub environment, Apple certificates,
Microsoft signing resources, and the existing Microsoft Store submission. Windows
Store MSIX drafts use the reserved identity and become Microsoft-signed only after
certification. They do not make the direct-download EXE signed or available.
Regression coverage: Infrastructure desktop status parser and navigation tests.

### Windows certification diagnostics

A Store draft validation retains the installed executable's embedded manifest,
process/window DPI awareness, and a compact list of non-passing WACK tests in
its validation artifact. Missing manifest-tool output is explicitly unavailable.
These receipts help distinguish packaging errors from certification-tool
warnings; they do not approve a package. The submission gate still requires an
overall WACK `PASS`, plus the existing runtime and publisher review gates.
Do not remove Flutter license notices or required plugin functionality merely to
hide an informational test. [Microsoft documents optional Desktop Bridge tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/uwp/debug-test-perf/windows-desktop-bridge-app-tests)
as informational, but a required DPI warning still needs investigation.

The Windows runner manifest declares both the legacy `dpiAware` value `true/pm`
and modern `dpiAwareness` value `PerMonitorV2`. [Microsoft documents both
manifest declarations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/application-manifests):
Windows 10 version 1607 and later uses the modern declaration in preference to
the legacy one. This preserves PerMonitorV2 while exposing the compatible legacy
fallback to older consumers.

A diagnostic report can still return overall `WARNING`: observed optional tests
flagged Flutter's compressed `NOTICES.Z` and process-launch references in bundled
binaries, while the required DPI test could not process the executable despite
its extracted PerMonitorV2 manifest and positive installed-process DPI receipt.
These are different findings. The dual declaration is a compatibility change,
not proof the certification warning is resolved. Require a fresh exact-source
Windows build, extracted manifest/runtime DPI checks, and overall WACK `PASS`
before submission. Preserve licenses and legitimate functionality while
investigating; do not convert warnings into passing results.


### Infrastructure desktop signing contract

The separate Infrastructure desktop contract admits only the direct
`desktop-beta.yaml` workflow on `production`, in the protected `desktop-beta`
environment, with audience `tuturuuu-desktop-deployment`. Signature, issuer,
subject, source SHA, numeric run/attempt, event and GitHub-hosted runner claims
are checked before credentials can be considered. Mobile store jobs, main-based
diagnostics, pull requests and unexpected reusable workflows are excluded.

Windows admits an Authenticode PFX and its password. macOS admits a **Developer
ID Application** P12, its password and signing identity, Apple team, and a separate
notarization P8 with App Store Connect key/issuer identifiers. Profile validation
rejects missing, duplicate, extra or other-platform resources. Public Flutter
configuration is a separate contract and never belongs in a signing bundle.
Linux and Store MSIX do not consume this signing bundle.

The desktop contract, encrypted storage, operator UI, protected bundle endpoint,
and runner hydration are implemented as separate layers. The existing mobile
vault is unchanged, and desktop publication remains opt-in. `desktopVaultEnabled`
requires an explicit `true`; implemented source does not establish provisioning,
certificate validity or signed runtime success.
`desktop-deployment/contract.test.ts` and `desktop-deployment/oidc.test.ts` cover
platform isolation and locally signed JWT rejection. Actual protected-workflow
OIDC, certificate identity, installation, WACK and update proof remain required.

### Private desktop vault storage

Desktop signing storage is additive and separate from the mobile vault. Windows
and macOS have independent draft versions and exact resource names; Linux and
Store MSIX drafts do not receive desktop signing bundles. Ordinary authenticated
and anonymous database roles cannot read encrypted resources, data keys or token
hashes. Service-only administration requires an explicit actor who belongs to the
root workspace and has `manage_desktop_deployment_vault` permission.

Each resource is encrypted with AES-GCM and authenticated against its desktop
version, platform and resource name. A replacement cannot transplant ciphertext
between platforms or versions. Draft writes increment the revision and invalidate
readiness; active resource values and encrypted data-key identity are immutable.
Validation and activation use the expected revision. Complete resource names are
a structural prerequisite, not proof of a valid signing certificate: the server's
certificate and platform readiness checks must succeed before it records a clean
validation result.

CI tokens contain only a stored hash and bind to a single platform and version.
The verified desktop OIDC run and attempt reserve a unique fetch lease before
decryption. Completion rechecks current admission, token expiry and revocation,
and the active version before any bundle may be returned. A delivered or failed
lease cannot replay; a lost response requires a new workflow run attempt. Audit
records use fixed event names and contain no credential values or exception text.

Both platform environments start disabled. Activating a ready version selects
immutable signing material; it does not enable delivery. The operator screen,
protected bundle endpoint and optional runner hydration are implemented in the
sections below. Environment-secret signing remains the default until
`DESKTOP_SIGNING_SOURCE=vault` is explicitly selected and the independent server
admission gates are enabled. None of these source layers establishes certificate
trust, artifact signing, notarization or installation proof.
Regression coverage: `desktop-deployment-vault.sql` tests permission boundaries,
platform separation, revision invalidation, immutable active bytes, replay and
revocation; `vault-crypto.test.ts` tests tamper and identity binding.

### Portable certificate readiness

Desktop vault readiness inspects the uploaded PKCS#12 material for one matching
private key and certificate, a current validity interval and an explicit
code-signing extended key usage. macOS additionally requires the Developer ID
Application extension, an exact configured common-name signing identity and a
matching team identifier. The notarization key must parse as a PKCS#8 EC P-256
private key. Rejections return fixed codes; passwords, private key bytes and
parser errors are never part of a readiness response. Successful responses contain
only a certificate fingerprint, expiry and algorithm.

These are portable material checks, not operating-system trust-chain or revocation
verification, Apple account access, notarization or artifact-signing proof. The
protected per-platform signing and verification workflow remains required before
publishing a downloadable artifact. The current PKCS#12 parser supports RSA
certificate bags; unsupported key/certificate material fails closed instead of
being described as ready. [Forge documents its PKCS#12 parser and unsupported-key behavior](https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge),
and [Apple documents the Developer ID Application certificate extension](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3127-inside-code-signing-requirements).
Regression coverage: `certificate-readiness.test.ts` uses freshly generated
synthetic material for key mismatch, missing keys, duplicate matches, validity,
code-signing, Developer ID identity/team and notarization-key boundaries.

### Private desktop administration API

Infrastructure's desktop administration API requires an authenticated registered
satellite actor, explicit root workspace MEMBER membership and the dedicated
`manage_desktop_deployment_vault` permission. Browser mutations additionally
require the exact local origin and desktop action header. JSON and multipart
uploads enforce actual streamed byte limits, including chunked uploads.

Responses expose version/revision/readiness metadata, configured resource names
and token identifiers only. Password suffixes, encrypted resources, data keys,
plaintext hashes and token hashes are excluded. A newly issued token is returned
once to its authorized creator and is never included in state reads.

Draft edits use expected revisions and invalidate readiness. Activation repeats
time-sensitive portable certificate checks before the atomic revision-fenced
activation RPC. Windows and macOS resource names cannot cross platforms. No version
operation enables a platform environment. Bundle delivery is independently
default-off; the operator UI and protected workflow hydration are implemented
separately. These endpoints alone do not establish signed delivery.
Regression coverage: desktop `access.test.ts`, `request.test.ts`,
`store.test.ts` and `mutations.test.ts`.

### Private desktop operator panel

Root workspace members can continue viewing public desktop deployment metadata.
Only the verified Infrastructure satellite actor with explicit MEMBER membership
and desktop vault permission sees signing administration. The desktop page uses
that actor for permission checks; personal and non-root redirects are preserved.

Windows and macOS drafts use empty replacement inputs and configured-name status
without saved-value readback. Activation requires current revision readiness and
still repeats certificate checks on the server. Operators can explicitly change platform admission with the audited controls
described below; the UI never changes the global delivery gate. Newly issued seven-day tokens are masked, shown once, discarded on
dismissal or actor/page lifetime changes, and cannot be recovered from state.
A definitive permission denial hides retained metadata; revision conflicts reload
current state while retaining the operator's replacement input for retry.

The client uses shared Internal API functions and actor-scoped TanStack Query
keys. This administration surface does not establish provider provisioning,
OS trust, WACK, signing, notarization or protected hydration success. Regression
coverage: `page-access.test.ts` and `desktop-vault-client.test.tsx`.

Private operator writes pass no credential variables into the shared TanStack
mutation cache and return no signing token as mutation data. The actor-local
operation publishes safe metadata and the one-time token separately; completion
and unmount clear the operation reference, and cache errors retain only a fixed
status/message. Cache regressions cover pending scalar/file writes, dismissal,
conflicts, logout and delayed old-actor completion.

## Protected desktop signing bundle

Infrastructure exposes a separate machine-only `POST /api/v1/desktop-deployment/bundle`
for Windows and macOS. `DESKTOP_DEPLOYMENT_VAULT_ENABLED` defaults off and the private
platform environment must independently be enabled. Operator activation selects an
immutable version; it never changes either admission switch. Metadata distinguishes
the global switch from platform admission as two independent badges on each platform,
including when only one is enabled, without exposing an enabling control. The
operator regression covers all four switch combinations. JSON requests may include
media-type parameters such as `application/json; charset=utf-8`; unrelated media
types are rejected before verification or service access.

The endpoint verifies the signed fixed desktop GitHub OIDC contract before token
lookup or service-client access. A hashed token binds platform and active version;
the private reserve RPC binds the verified run, attempt and source SHA. Exact
resource names, encrypted identities, fresh portable certificate/P8 readiness and
a final live revocation/expiry/version check precede response. Failed or delivered
leases cannot be reused, including after a response is lost; a new workflow attempt
is required. Signing buffers are wiped on success and failure.

This endpoint supplies the optional runner hydrator described below. It does not
enable any environment, provision credentials, establish OS trust or prove
artifact signing/notarization. Linux and Store MSIX diagnostics do not fetch this
bundle. Mobile trust remains independent.
Regression coverage lives in the desktop `bundle-store.test.ts`, bundle route tests
and operator admission-badge cases; previous actual lease SQL and signed OIDC tests
remain the storage and signature boundaries.

### Infrastructure vault runner opt-in

Desktop beta signing uses the existing environment secrets by default. An operator
can explicitly select `DESKTOP_SIGNING_SOURCE=vault` as a repository variable and
configure separate `DESKTOP_WINDOWS_VAULT_CI_TOKEN` and
`DESKTOP_MACOS_VAULT_CI_TOKEN` environment secrets. This selects the protected
Infrastructure bundle endpoint only for the matching production desktop-beta job
after Flutter compilation. It does not enable the server vault or either platform;
all existing server admission gates still apply. A rejected or unavailable bundle
blocks that platform without falling back to legacy credentials. Linux packaging
and Store MSIX diagnostics never request this bundle.

The runner imports the same pure signing profile allowlist as Infrastructure,
checks schema, platform, resource names, canonical base64, SHA-256 and byte bounds,
and passes only matching material to a short-lived signing child. No credential
is written to `GITHUB_ENV`, outputs, public build configuration, or artifact paths.
Wire-valid resources must also fit a conservative 30,000-byte whole-child
environment budget; oversized certificates/scalars block before signing rather
than claiming the 2 MiB storage limit is an OS environment guarantee.
Private signer files use a separate owned directory (0700 on macOS; inherited ACLs
removed and runner-principal access granted on Windows) while public artifact paths
remain unchanged. Normal completion and failures remove that directory. Cancellation force-stops
only the still-owned signing process tree before cleanup; POSIX uses one immediate
process-group kill, avoiding a delayed kill after the parent exits. JavaScript
strings and abrupt runner termination cannot promise memory erasure; the hosted
runner lifecycle remains the final boundary. Child output is suppressed and only
fixed failure messages are emitted. Bundle requests are not retried because lease
consumption deliberately binds one run attempt.

Regression coverage: `scripts/desktop-deployment/vault-hydrator.test.mjs` verifies
exact projection/hash/stream bounds, protected runner admission, fixed destination,
secret-free child environment, private-directory cleanup and post-compile opt-in.
These tests do not prove Windows ACL behavior, real GitHub OIDC, signing trust,
notarization, or protected production configuration. The workflow's actual Node 24
and operating-system jobs remain required delivery evidence. See the
[Node TypeScript runtime](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/typescript.html)
and [Windows ACL command contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/icacls).

### Audited platform admission control

The Infrastructure desktop administration API accepts `enable_delivery` and
`disable_delivery` for Windows and macOS. Both require same-origin operator
mutation admission, explicit root `MEMBER` membership, the desktop vault permission,
and the current `environmentRevision`. Enabling also names the active version and
its validated revision; the server decrypts and verifies the exact profile, fresh
certificate validity, and macOS P8 material before issuing its short-lived internal
receipt. Browser credentials or readiness receipts cannot authorize enabling.
Disabling needs no credential inspection, so unavailable or expired material does
not prevent an operator from stopping delivery. Version activation still does not
enable a platform. No operation changes `DESKTOP_DEPLOYMENT_VAULT_ENABLED`, which
remains an independent global default-off gate.

Each successful platform control writes an actor audit event and advances the
environment revision. Bundle reservation captures that revision; final delivery
rejects older reservations after disable, re-enable, or active-version changes.
Pre-migration leases with revision `-1` cannot deliver. The existing token,
environment, then lease lock order remains intact. During additive-schema rollout,
metadata reports a missing revision as `null`; clients must reload a real revision
before offering a control. Source availability does not establish activation,
OS trust, signing, provisioning, or publication proof.

Server-page fixtures mock the current `getDesktopPageAccess` boundary and return
its admitted actor and management permission. Do not mock a superseded root guard
or suppress `server-only` globally to make page tests import. `page.test.tsx` covers
access-before-metadata ordering and member-versus-manager controls;
`page-access.test.ts` independently covers the real satellite actor, root membership
and permission checks.

Regression coverage: `desktop-deployment-admission.sql` exercises permission, CAS,
freshness, disable/re-enable and legacy-lease denial; `admission.test.ts` and
`request.test.ts` cover credential-free disable, trusted receipts, fresh material,
sanitized failures, and strict browser inputs.

The operator panel offers a confirmation before enabling platform admission. It
requires the environment's real revision and matching validated active version;
missing rollout metadata, stale actor refreshes, or an in-flight mutation disable
controls. Disable remains available without active credentials and while the
global gate is off. Both controls use the actor-local mutation boundary, reload
on revision conflicts, and discard late results after actor changes. A changed
environment revision or active version dismisses an old confirmation. The
independent gate badges remain visible for all four global/platform combinations.
`desktop-vault-client.test.tsx` exercises real QueryClient confirmation, CAS,
credential-free disable, concurrent dispatch, and actor-ABA publication.

### Private macOS signing failure diagnostics

The macOS signer captures child output privately. Failed `codesign` commands
publish only an allowlisted category, artifact kind and bounded numeric exit
status, alongside the fixed signing stage. Categories cover keychain access,
identity availability, certificate trust, unsigned components, bundle format,
resource metadata and timestamp availability; unmatched output is `unknown`.
Paths, signing identities, command arguments, raw output and private inputs never
become public error details. This classification preserves failure, cleanup,
strict signature/team verification and required notarization gates. It improves
next-run diagnosis without establishing or repairing the original signing cause.
Regression coverage includes real failing child processes, private-output
suppression and failure cleanup in `sign-macos.test.mjs`, plus the finite
classification contract in `codesign-diagnostic.test.mjs`.
